newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Strangles bought in Glaxo Wellcome.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Strangles bought in Glaxo Wellcome.

text.p: Trading activity in UK stock options moderated on Thursday as traders took a cautiously optimistic view of the market, dealers said.

Pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome attracted the attention of one trader who bought strangles in the options. The deal was to buy 1,250 October 1150 puts at about 49p as well as 1,250 October 1200 calls at about 66p.
The deal will make money if volatility increases for the stock such that the shares either go below 1035p or above 1315p by expiry.
At 1450 GMT, Glaxo Wellcome shares were 7p up at 1195p.
In conglomerate Lonrho a short put position was rolled forward and it involved buying back 522 June 160 puts at about 22p and 567 September 160 puts sold at about 23p.

Elsewhere, in the tobacco sector the main deal involved two stock option classes. It concerned one trader selling 500 November 260 puts at 11-1/2p in Gallaher Group and also buying 350 November 360 puts at 12p in Imperial Tobacco implying a belief that Gallaher shares will stay above 260p by expiry and Imperial's to go below 360p.
Gallaher shares fell 2p to 275-1/2p while Imperial Tobacco was up 4-1/2p to 385p.
Over in FTSE 100 index options the main deals were volatility trades which involve taking up an options position which is suitably hedged by an opposite deal in FTSE futures.

The biggest of these was from a buyer of 4,000 July 4425 puts at prices between 46p to 47-1/2p against buying June futures at 4550 so that increased market volatility will turn the deal into profit. At 1450 GMT, cash FTSE was up 14.1 at 4571.2 while June futures were up 16 at 4568.
